titles.728: Annotatio VI §.VII open: Wittenberger — Indigni Oral as proof presence is not imaginary
titles.729: Annotatio VI §.VII: is spiritual presence mere imagination? Faith then empty?
titles.730: Annotatio VI §.VII: presence common to unfaithful and faithful vs faithful-only?
titles.731: Annotatio VI §.VII press: if Indignorum doctrine is slight, why Paul’s solicitude?
titles.732: Annotatio VI §.VII reply: Paul never teaches Impious eat Christ’s body — he guards against it
titles.733: Annotatio VI §.VII: Indigni eat panem Domini (bread of Lord), not panem Dominum (Lord-bread)

latin.728: §. VII. Ceterum Clariss. Wittebergensis non in nuda assertione Manducationis corporis Christi Corporalis, indignis competentis, acquiescit, sed Necessitatem ac Fundamentalitatem quoque, quoad fidem Christianam, Assertionis illi, per id, conciliare studet, quòd fortius nihil opinatur esse, ad evincendum, præsentiam corporis Christi non esse relativam aut merè imaginariam, quæ fide & cogitatione fiat, quam si doceatur, etiam indignos & fidei expertes, corpus & sanguinem Christi percipere §. XII.
latin.729: Ergone Clarissimus Auctor Spiritualem Christi corporísque ejus & sanguinis præsentiam, (quâ is fidelium suorum animabus, cum in Cœna S. tùm extra eam, ineffabili modo præsentissimus est, caro ejus, istarum verus cibus, nutriens eas ad vitam æternam, sanguis ejus verus potus, purgans earum conscientias à pravis operibus ad inseriendum Vero uni DEO) merè imaginariam sibi imaginatur, omnis realitatis & veritatis expertem? Næ ipse FIDEM, per quam unam, CHRISTUS membris suis, & hæc CHRISTO, arctissimè uniuntur, admodum jejunam & otiosam concipit!
latin.730: Aut realioremne veriorémque præsentiam istam Christi ejusque corporis & sanguinis arbitrabitur A., infidelibus fidelibúsque juxta communem, quam Fidelibus solis propriam? Næ, sic profitebitur, vix se gustasse & adhuc dum percepisse, quam acceptus Dominus iis sit, qui fide vivâ illi adhærent!
latin.731: At instat Autor, Necessitatem doctrinæ de indignorum manducatione corporis Christi sustentaturus: Quodsi, ait, in doctrina de Manducatione indignorum parum aut nihil situm est, cur eam Paulus tantâ sollicitudine curáque explicuit? Numne credibile, Apostolum exigui momenti rem, tantô studio persecuturum fuisse?
latin.732: Resp. Apostolus nullibi, vel syllaba una, Manducationem corporis Christi ab indignis fieri explicuit, quin potiùs indignorum manducationem in S. Cœna commemoraturus, omni sollicitudine & curâ cavet, ne quis opinetur, indignos corpus Christi manducare.
latin.733: Eóque manducationis, in legitimo S. Cœnæ usu, Objectum dimidiatum duntaxat minusque principale, scilicet panem solum, indignorum causâ, inducit, ita scribens: Quoties de pane hoc ederitis & de poculo hoc biberitis, mortem Domini annuntiabitis, donec redeat. Quicunque igitur indignè de PANE HOC manducat, is reus sit Corporis Christi: Indeque exploret Seipsum homo, & ita edat de pane hoc, & bibat de poculo hoc. Nimirum, hoc Doctrinæ caput de Indignorum Manducatione panis istius, qui Domini est, non autem panis illius, qui Dominus ipse est, rectius ac evidentius multo, quam (quod Auctor vult) caput doctrinæ, de Indignorum Manducatione corporis Christi Orali.
latin.734: Veram realémque præsentiam corporis & sanguinis Christi in S. Cœna, istam scilicet confirmat, cujus Fideles manducando redduntur participes, Infideles, panem licèt Domini manducantes, expertes tamen manent; à securitate etiam Carnali homines retrahit, ne sibi imaginentur, se Christi corporis participes fieri posse, in spurcissimis utut peccatis volutati; de Charitatis divinæ erga se abundantia convincit pios, quâ illis filii sui carnem vivificantem, in pignus paterni amoris, impertit, impiis, ceu supposititiis, eâdem jure meritóque denegatâ; Denique ad veram seriamque pœnitentiam, sicque ad usum Cœnæ frequentiorem invitat, utpote citra quam pœnitentiam, nulla carnis Christi vivificantis participatio speranda est — obtinenda autem tantò copiosius, quantò frequentiùs verâ pœnitentiâ & fide instructus quispiam, S. Domini Cœnam accedit.

pass_a.728: §. VII. Moreover the most distinguished Wittenberger does not rest in the bare assertion of Corporal Eating of Christ’s body as belonging to the unworthy, but also strives to win Necessity and Fundamentality, as to Christian faith, for that Assertion — by this: that he thinks nothing stronger for proving that Christ’s body’s presence is not relative or merely imaginary, made by faith and thought, than if it be taught that even the unworthy and those without faith perceive Christ’s body and blood (§. XII).
pass_a.729: Does the most distinguished Author therefore imagine to himself the Spiritual presence of Christ and of his body and blood — by which he is most present in an ineffable mode to his faithful’s souls, both in the Holy Supper and outside it, his flesh their true food nourishing them to eternal life, his blood true drink purging their consciences from dead works to serve the one true GOD — as merely imaginary, void of all reality and truth? Nay, he himself conceives FAITH, by which alone CHRIST is most tightly united to his members and they to CHRIST, as quite jejune and idle!
pass_a.730: Or will the Author judge that presence of Christ and of his body and blood common alike to unfaithful and faithful more real and truer than that proper to the Faithful alone? Nay, so professing, he will scarcely have tasted and even now perceived how acceptable the Lord is to those who cling to him by living faith!
pass_a.731: But the Author presses, about to sustain the Necessity of the doctrine of the unworthy’s eating of Christ’s body: But if, he says, little or nothing is placed in the doctrine of the Eating of the unworthy, why did Paul explain it with such solicitude and care? Is it credible that the Apostle would have pursued a matter of slight moment with such zeal?
pass_a.732: Reply: The Apostle nowhere, even by one syllable, explained that Eating of Christ’s body is done by the unworthy — nay rather, when about to mention the unworthy’s eating in the Holy Supper, he with all solicitude and care bewares lest anyone opine that the unworthy eat Christ’s body.
pass_a.733: And so, for the unworthy’s sake, he introduces only a halved and less principal Object of eating in the legitimate use of the Holy Supper — namely bread alone — writing thus: As often as you eat of this bread and drink of this cup, you will announce the Lord’s death until he return. Whoever therefore eats unworthily of THIS BREAD, he is guilty of Christ’s Body: And thence let a man examine Himself, and so eat of this bread, and drink of this cup. To be sure, this head of Doctrine concerning the Unworthy’s Eating of that bread which is of the Lord, not of that bread which is the Lord himself, much more rightly and evidently than (what the Author wills) the head of doctrine concerning Oral Eating of Christ’s body by the Unworthy.
pass_a.734: Confirms that true and real presence of Christ’s body and blood in the Holy Supper of which the Faithful by eating are made partakers, while the Unfaithful, though eating the bread of the Lord, remain without share; it also pulls men back from Carnal security, lest they imagine they can become partakers of Christ’s body while wallowing in the foulest sins; it convicts the pious of the abundance of divine Charity toward them, by which He imparts his Son’s vivifying flesh as pledge of fatherly love, the same justly denied to the Impious as counterfeits; Finally it invites to true serious repentance and so to more frequent use of the Supper — inasmuch as without that repentance no participation of Christ’s vivifying flesh is to be hoped — and to be obtained all the more richly the more often anyone instructed with true repentance and faith approaches the Lord’s Holy Supper.

728: §.VII: the Wittenberger will not stop at bare assertion that the unworthy corporally eat Christ’s body.

He also tries to make that claim necessary and faith-fundamental — thinking nothing stronger proves presence is not relative or imaginary than teaching that even the faithless perceive body and blood (§.XII).
729: So is spiritual presence of Christ, body, and blood — most present to faithful souls in and beyond the Supper, true food and drink unto eternal life — mere imagination void of reality?
Then he empties FAITH itself, the one bond by which Christ and his members are tightly united.
730: Or is a presence shared by unfaithful and faithful alike more real than the presence proper to the faithful alone?
Anyone who says so has barely tasted how welcome the Lord is to those who cling by living faith.
731: He presses necessity: if the Indignorum doctrine matters little, why did Paul treat it with such care?
Would the Apostle chase a slight matter with that zeal?
732: Reply: Paul nowhere, not by a syllable, teaches that the unworthy eat Christ’s body.
When he mentions unworthy eating in the Supper, he carefully guards lest anyone think they eat the body.
733: For their sake he names only the lesser object — this bread — “whoever eats this bread unworthily is guilty of the body”; examine yourself, then eat and drink.
So the true head is Indigni eating the bread of the Lord, not the bread that is the Lord — clearer than the Author’s Oral-body-of-Indigni head.
734: That doctrine confirms real presence for faithful partakers; the unfaithful may eat the Lord’s bread and still remain without share.

It pulls men from carnal security, shows the pious the Father’s gift of vivifying flesh, denies it to the Impious as counterfeits, and invites true repentance and frequent worthy approach. Stop §.VII before §.VIII.

notes.729: Spiritual presence not imaginary; faith not empty.
notes.732: Paul never teaches Impious eat the body.
notes.734: Fruits of true Indignorum head; before §.VIII.
